'''Peter Charles Howard Pritchard'''<ref name=EDR/> (June 26, 1943 – February 25, 2020) was a leading [[cheloniologist|turtle zoologist]]. Pritchard was educated at [[Oxford University]] and the [[University of Florida]], where he received a Ph.D. and specialized in Zoology. He was most commonly known for his career of almost 40 years for the conservation of turtles.

He worked with the World Wildlife Fund, spending four years there before joining Audubon Florida in 1973 as assistant executive director, senior vice president and acting president. In 1997,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-02-27|title=Turtle conservationist Peter Pritchard dies at 76|url=https://www.kaieteurnewsonline.com/2020/02/27/turtle-conservationist-peter-pritchard-dies-at-76/|access-date=2021-01-12|website=Kaieteur News|language=en-US}}</ref> he founded a turtle conservation organization called the Chelonian Research Institute in [[Oviedo, Florida]]. [[Scott A. Thomson]], curator of the Chelonian Research Institute notes that the CRI has 14500 tortoise and turtle specimens registered with some 2000 unregistered specimens. The collection comprises 100% of all turtle genera, 86% of all species and 72% of all subspecies - the third largest and most complete collection in the world.

Pritchard also travelled to [[Guyana]] for his career, the [[South America]]n country that is home to four of the world's seven known [[sea turtle]] species: the [[leatherback turtle|leatherback]], [[green sea turtle|green]], [[hawksbill turtle|hawksbill]] and the [[olive ridley turtle|olive ridley]]. He also named several species of turtle for example ''[[Mesoclemmys zuliae]]'' and ''[[Chitra vandijki]]''. He also worked with the [[Lokono]] during his turtle conservation experience in Guyana.

Along the way, Pritchard's own scholarship has benefited from centuries' worth of tribal turtle knowledge. He has also done extensive study and written books about [[alligator snapping turtle]]s and [[Galapagos tortoise]]s.

Pritchard died on February 25, 2020.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Florida scientist Peter Pritchard, known as ‘the Turtle God,’ dies at 76|url=https://www.tampabay.com/news/environment/2020/02/28/florida-scientist-peter-pritchard-known-as-the-turtle-god-dies-at-76/|access-date=2021-01-12|website=Tampa Bay Times|language=en}}</ref>

==Eponyms==
Pritchard is honored in the [[Binomial nomenclature|scientific names]] of three turtles, ''Podocnemis pritchardi'' {{extinct}},<ref name = Wood>Wood RC (1997). "Turtles". '''In:''' Kay RF, Madden RH, Cifelli RL,  Flynn JJ (editors). ''Vertebrate Paleontology in the Neotropics. The Miocene Fauna of La Venta, Colombia''. Washington, District of Columbia: Smithsonian Institution Press.</ref> ''[[Chelodina pritchardi]]'' and ''[[Mauremys pritchardi]]''.<ref name=EDR>Beolens, Bo; Watkins, Michael; Grayson, Michael (2011). ''The Eponym Dictionary of Reptiles''. Baltimore: Johns Hopkins University Press. xiii + 296 pp. {{ISBN|978-1-4214-0135-5}}. ("Pritchard", pp. 211-212).</ref>
